name: Yunus Emre
bio: Yunus Emre is the first recorded native poet of the Western Turks: a mystic who wrote in Anatolian Turkish rather than in the Persian forms that Ottoman court poets later preferred. Ottoman biographers describe him as nearly unlettered, a disciple of the holy man Tapduk Emre, whose verse was held to be a direct gift of God.

Only a little is known of his life, and the early sources disagree. E. J. W. Gibb, whose History of Ottoman Poetry (1900) gives the first English account of him, notes that one of his own poems dates his devotion to the Path to the year 707 AH (1307–8), which places him about a century before the dates given by later biographers.

poems.title: Faith, Idol, Ka'ba-Fane Am I
poems.author: Yunus Emre
poems.collection: A History of Ottoman Poetry, vol. I (1900)
poems.note: A pantheistic ghazel in which the poet identifies himself with God and with all of creation. Gibb's notes explain the Qur'anic and Islamic allusions in the lines.

poems.title: That Mighty One of 'Be! and 'Tis
poems.author: Yunus Emre
poems.collection: A History of Ottoman Poetry, vol. I (1900)
poems.note: A ghazel built on the Qur'anic phrase 'Be! and it is', in which the poet speaks as God's creative power. Gibb's notes explain the allusions to the Light verse of the Qur'an and to the divine command.

poems.title: Come and Let Us Two Be Comrades
poems.author: Yunus Emre
poems.collection: A History of Ottoman Poetry, vol. I (1900)
poems.note: A short invitation from the poet to a friend to set out together on the mystic path, in search of the Beloved. Gibb's notes explain that the 'Friend' and the 'Loved One' mean God.
